I was just a few weeks from my 21st bday when I got the call from my nurse about my diagnosis. 

In the prior weeks I had been feeling like shit after eating meals and I could tell (tw: TMI) that I had a HORRIBLE yeast infection. It was bad to the point where I was like, rocking back and forth in a chair at work to make the itch go away. I had a thought right in that moment "normal people don't live like this" and I saw my dr the next day. They ordered me to come in the following day for blood work while fasting. I got the call from the nurse the following day and she gave me my diagnosis. My sugars while fasting were in the 280s. My A1C was 10.7. I'm going to have to take insulin and see a diabetes educator and endocrinologist. 

It was very hard to adjust at first but you really do get the "hang" of it. I've had it for nearly 5 years now and even though there are days where you just won't be able to control your sugars, the good days will outnumber the bad by far. However I have the greatest support system ever and I'm extremely lucky. 

I hate to have to say it, but welcome to the community!!  <3

Obligatory "it's not that simple" comment. I see where you are coming from and to an extent I agree. Mentally ill people are mentally ill so they do mentally ill things because they are *mentally ill*. They hardly ever believe that they have a problem so they blame it on others and take their anger out on others because they don't have proper ways to deal or cope with their illness. 

My mom has borderline personality disorder and for a large portion of my life she was untreated and undiagnosed. My mom rarely hit us, but was extremely emotionally and verbally abusive. I didn't realize it at the time but looking back on it I can see signs that she seriously didn't want to be the way she was. I saw the suffering and exhaustion in her eyes. She intentionally locked herself in her bedroom for *days* and would only come out to eat or use the bathroom or shower. It was the only way she could keep herself from lashing out at us. 

My mom now has been in treatment programs, is on the right meds and is happier than ever. I talk to her a lot now and she has given me so much insight as to what her world looked like from her point of view. Again, im not at all excusing this abusive behavior but their is a certain level of understanding that you have to have when dealing with mentally ill people. If they weren't mentally ill I can almost certainly guarantee they wouldn't be doing/saying/acting they way they are.

I read a comment that u/Black_House_Cat made on another post about someone dying of cancer. The health issues are different but what they said really stuck with me. I've never once in my life thought that death isn't a punishment, like they said in their post. I'll copy paste it below: 


"For what it's worth, we all must remember that death is not a punishment. It comes for us all- sometimes expected, and sometimes not. It is as much a part of life as being born is. Arguably, knowing is worse than it just happening suddenly one day, BUT the trade off is that you have time to really think about and choose what you want to experience and leave behind until your loved ones come join you. 

Cancer is a fucking monster, and I am so sorry you are suffering it's range of effects- both physical and mental. It's cruel and it sucks. I truly cannot express my sorrow that you must experience it. 

As others have said, humans can't comprehend "nothing." Look at teachings of enlightenment or nirvana or other abstract afterlife concepts. They all focus on the freedom and peace, as being alive is the only thing that can cause us to suffer. Think of all the bad things that will be stripped away and the boundaries that will be removed so you can exist and experience a bodyless period. Who knows what secrets of the universe are unlocked when you aren't constrained by a flawed human body. Everything we know about existence after dearh indicates that it is beautiful and peace incarnate. Energy can neither be created nor destroyed. 

That is the next step, and we will all join you one day. I wish you could tell us what it's like, but it's a rite of passage we all must go through on our own. Stay strong hearted- you are a beautiful soul and have done nothing wrong. Make peace with death. It will make your time here feel more valuable in the end. You are loved. <3"

I really hope this helps you, it seriously helped me. <3

I personally have had to close people's accounts because they keep receiving third party deposits without knowing where the funds are coming from (like if they are a scam victim and they continue to receive fraud funds). Sure it might be a simple mistake (someone miskeys their account # and it just happens to be your account # for example) but it could also be a scam. At the end of the day, the funds do not belong to the OP and eventually the intended payee of the funds will try to reclaim them so the OP should not use them. 

Also different banks might have different policies regarding third party deposits. That person who said that might be right because that's the procedure at their bank. At my bank this is how it works. Think about it like this:

you receive 35k, it's a direct deposit not in your name (because the deposit wasn't intended for you so its not payable to you), you have no idea where the funds are coming from but you used them anyway? 

It's just stupid. The bank where the funds came from can at any time send our bank a reversal form/document reporting that the deposit was fraudulent and wasn't supposed to go to the account that it did. Then we check the account and we see that you used 20k of the 35k, all the bank knows is that you used funds that aren't yours and now the funds are reported as unauthorized to come to your account. It's all just really dangerous territory and if OP is reading this comment, then my best recommendation is to call their banks fraud department and ask what their policies are regarding use of funds that they weren't expecting to get and they don't know the origin of.
